name: VPN Support
tagline: Subscription VPN endpoints for the providers you choose
description: Add VPN endpoints to the exit set of the providers or pools you list. Paste a subscription (or a node URI), pick how many IPs to keep and how they are used, and the gateway takes care of the rest: it fetches the subscription, parses every endpoint, probes it, keeps the best ones and drops the ones that stopped answering, then repeats on the configured refresh interval so expired subscriptions are replaced automatically. Turn on Keep working IPs and the extension also keeps its own list of the IPs that answered: they are re-checked on every refresh, so a subscription update that replaces them does not lose the exit — an IP leaves that list only when it stops answering. Each endpoint list can be bound to several providers or pools at once. This extension ships only its own runtime and UI addons — no gateway code is required for it to work.
author: aurora

ui.help: Paste a subscription, choose how many IPs to keep, pick where they sit in the exit rotation and list the providers or pools they apply to (comma-separated). Turn on Keep working IPs to keep the IPs that answered in the extension's own list — they survive a subscription update and leave it only when they stop answering. Everything else has a working default.

fields.label: Subscriptions
fields.description: One per line: a subscription URL, a node URI pasted as-is, or a bare token when a subscription base URL is set.

fields.label: IPs to keep
fields.description: How many of the probed IPs to keep. 0 keeps all.

fields.label: Keep working IPs
fields.description: off — only the IPs the current subscriptions list. pool — the IPs that answered are saved in the extension's own working list and re-checked on every refresh, so a subscription update that replaces them does not lose the exit. pin — the saved IPs also keep their place in the exit rotation, and the new ones only fill the free slots.

fields.label: Exit mode
fields.description: rotate — with the provider's own source addresses. fallback — only after they fail or hit a rate limit. vpn_only — these first, source addresses last.

fields.label: Providers and pools
fields.description: Comma-separated provider or pool names this list binds to, for example opencode-zen, backup. * applies everywhere.

fields.label: Auto-fetch interval (minutes)
fields.description: How often subscriptions are re-read and IPs re-probed, in minutes. 0 disables it.

fields.label: Working list size
fields.description: How many saved IPs the working list holds. 0 keeps all of them.

fields.label: Misses before a drop
fields.description: How many refreshes in a row a saved IP may not answer before it leaves the working list.

fields.label: Selection order
fields.description: Sort the probed IPs by latency: best first, worst first, or shuffled.

fields.label: Quality threshold (ms)
fields.description: IPs slower than this are dropped. 0 keeps every IP that answers.

fields.label: Local SOCKS ports
fields.description: Local SOCKS ports for the tunnel core. Leave the default single port and the range sizes itself to how many endpoints are kept (1080, 1081, …, one per kept endpoint — including node_count 0 = keep all, after every refresh). List two or more ports to pin the set exactly.

fields.label: Tunnel core
fields.description: none: report endpoints only, no local ports expected. static: you run the core listening on the port range shown on the Status tab (one port per kept endpoint). singbox: the gateway switches the active endpoint through the core's Clash API.

fields.label: Protocols
fields.description: Comma-separated protocols to keep, for example vless,vmess,ss,trojan.

fields.label: Regions to keep
fields.description: Comma-separated region/name fragments to keep. Empty keeps everything.

fields.label: Regions to drop
fields.description: Comma-separated region/name fragments to drop.

fields.label: Probe samples
fields.description: Number of connection attempts per IP; the median is used.

fields.label: Probe timeout (ms)
fields.description: Per-sample connection timeout. IPs that never answer are removed.

fields.label: Subscription base URL
fields.description: Optional. A bare token on the Subscriptions line is appended to this URL, so the list can hold only the token. Leave empty when every entry is already a full URL or a node URI.

fields.label: Subscription headers
fields.description: Optional JSON object of HTTP headers sent when fetching subscriptions, for example {"Authorization":"Bearer …"}.

fields.label: Core HTTP API
fields.description: Base URL of the core's control API, for example http://127.0.0.1:9090.

fields.label: Core API secret
fields.description: Optional bearer token for the core's control API.

fields.label: Core selector group
fields.description: Proxy group or outbound tag the endpoint is switched on.

items: Exit mode decides where these IPs sit: with the provider's own source addresses (rotate), behind them (fallback) or in front of them (vpn_only).
Subscriptions are re-read on the auto-fetch interval, so expired endpoints are replaced automatically.
Keep working IPs saves the IPs that answered in the extension's own list: they are re-checked on every refresh and an IP a subscription update drops keeps working until it stops answering.
Settings live in Settings → Extensions → VPN support.

requirements: A tunnel core listening on the local ports listed in the extension settings, unless core_kind is none
Local source addresses configured on each provider (bind_ips) if you want them mixed into or preferred over the endpoints
notes: This extension only contributes exits; it does not change how the gateway talks to providers.
Subscription URLs, headers and the core API secret are stored in the gateway's extension config.
The working list of the remembered IPs is kept in the extension's own state file next to the addon.
Review third-party extensions before installing them from a store.
